grader.scenario: Multi-Room TV whole-home recording sharing desynchronized with error MR-SYNC-404; resolved via MoCA 2.5 cluster re-keying; two handled outbursts; grand finale call
grader.notes: Grand finale call: flawless 100/100 support call featuring two handled outbursts with deep empathy, remote MoCA cluster re-keying, harmless recheck in final third, and complete multi-room live playback verification.

items.name: Branding and Survey Check
items.evidence: Agent opened with 'Thank you for calling S-Net TV technical support' at [00:00] and closed with 'Thank you for choosing S-Net' in final lines.

items.name: Hold time and Dead Air
items.evidence: Hold was announced with could I place you on hold and thanked upon return without unmanaged dead air.

items.name: Verified customer
items.evidence: Verified full postal address and security PIN within the first 240 seconds.

items.name: Personalized the call/ticket appropriately
items.evidence: Agent addressed customer as Zachary throughout the call.

items.name: Empathy & Acknowledgment Statement
items.evidence: Agent handled two separate customer emotional outbursts with profound empathy and reassuring warmth at turns 16 and 22, and no unhandled outbursts occurred.

items.name: Paraphrasing
items.evidence: Agent accurately paraphrased the multi-room whole-home recording sharing desynchronization issue at turn 2.

items.name: Active listening
items.evidence: Agent completed harmless recheck of customer address at turn 42.

items.name: Took ownership of the problem
items.evidence: Agent executed MoCA cluster re-keying, locked cluster encryption keys, and verified multiple mini boxes live on call.

items.name: Build rapport and observed professionalism
items.evidence: Agent maintained an exemplary, warm, and highly supportive professional demeanor throughout.

items.name: Probing
items.evidence: Agent probed about coaxial MoCA cabling versus Wi-Fi connectivity.

items.name: Confirmed the issue is resolved
items.evidence: Customer tested both bedroom mini boxes live on call, loaded full recording library, and streamed Doctor Who smoothly at 850 Mbps.
